title: Pressure-cooker mashed potato
subtitle: Fluffy, buttery mash ready in 10 minutes
excerpt: Floury potatoes cooked under pressure in 6 minutes, then riced into the silkiest mash. The pressure cooker cooks them faster and more evenly than boiling, with no waterlogging.
sourceNotes: Mashed potato is documented across European cuisines from the 18th century. The method of ricing cooked potatoes, pressing through a potato ricer rather than mashing, produces a lighter, lump-free result and is standard in French cuisine.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mash does not hold well; make and serve straight away. You can cook the potatoes up to 30 minutes ahead and keep them in the warm pot.

content.text: Pressure-cooker mashed potato is faster and better than the boiled version. The potatoes steam in about 6 minutes rather than 20. Steam-cooked potatoes do not waterlog. They come out dry and starchy, ready to absorb butter and cream without turning gluey.

Floury potatoes are essential, King Edward, Maris Piper, or Desiree. Waxy varieties, such as Charlotte or Jersey Royal, do not mash well; they turn into a gluey paste rather than the fluffy, aerated result that a floury potato produces.

A potato ricer gives the best result: no lumps, no overworking of the starch, and a light, even texture. A standard masher works if you do not have one, but work the mash as little as possible once the butter and cream go in.

Add 250 ml of water to the pressure cooker and place the trivet inside. Put the peeled, quartered potatoes on the trivet. Seal the lid and bring to high pressure. Cook at high pressure for 6 minutes, then quick-release.

Tip the potatoes into a warm bowl. Rice them immediately while hot, cold potatoes become gluey when riced. Add the cold butter cubes and stir through until melted. Warm {{whole-milk}} of milk and add gradually, stirring gently after each addition, until you reach the consistency you want. Season well with salt and pepper.

rows.symptom: The mash is gluey or sticky
rows.cause: Waxy potatoes were used, or the mash was overworked with an electric mixer.
rows.fix: For mash, use only floury varieties and mash by hand. Electric mixers break down the starch cells and release a sticky paste. Rest and restart with the right potato next time.

rows.symptom: The potatoes are still firm after 6 minutes
rows.cause: Very large chunks were used, or the pressure cooker did not reach full pressure.
rows.fix: Quarter the potatoes to roughly equal pieces, no larger than 4 cm. Cook at pressure for a further 3 minutes.

rows.cause: The potatoes were not fully cooked, or were mashed while slightly cool.
rows.fix: Mash potatoes immediately when they come out of the pressure cooker while piping hot. A potato ricer removes the risk of lumps entirely.

content.text: Good mashed potato is one of the most useful things in British cooking. It is the base for shepherd's pie, the side for sausages and gravy, and the foil for braised meats. The pressure cooker saves time without changing the result. The dry-steam method means the mash can take more butter and cream before it turns heavy.
